I've found two bugs in the Excalidraw codebase that need to be fixed.

*   AnimationController.start(key, callback) must invoke the callback synchronously on the first frame immediately upon being called.

*   When the callback passed to AnimationController.start returns { keep: true }, the animation continues and the next frame is scheduled.

*   When the callback passed to AnimationController.start returns null, the animation stops and the key is removed from the set of running animations.

*   AnimationController.running(key) must return false after an animation associated with that key has naturally ended (callback returned null) or been cancelled.

*   AnimationController.cancel(key) must stop a running animation; after cancellation a new animation can be successfully started with a different key.

*   When all animations have stopped or been cancelled and no frames are pending, there must be no remaining scheduled timers.

*   When updateScene is called with a collaborators map containing an entry whose pointer has tool set to 'laser' and button set to 'down', a path element must appear in the SVG layer of the canvas.

*   When updateScene is called with an empty collaborators map (all collaborators removed), all laser trail path elements previously rendered for remote collaborators must be removed from the SVG layer.


*   Interface details: Type: Class
Name: AnimationController
Location: packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts
Description: Static class that manages multiple named animations. Provides methods to start, cancel, and query animations by string key. Each animation runs frame by frame via a callback that controls continuation.
Signature:
  static start(key: string, callback: (frame: { state: any }) => { keep: true } | null): void
  static cancel(key: string): void
  static running(key: string): boolean


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

I fixed both bugs in source files only. Typecheck passes and the existing laser tests still pass.

## Bug 1 — `AnimationController` (`packages/excalidraw/renderer/animation.ts`)

The old code used a bare `isRunning` boolean and never stored the scheduled timer handle. This caused two failures:

- **Stuck flag / broken restart:** After `cancel()` (or when a tick drained the map to empty), `isRunning` stayed `true` with no frame actually scheduled. A subsequent `start()` saw `isRunning === true` and skipped scheduling, so the new animation never ticked.
- **Dangling timers:** `cancel()` only deleted the map entry — it never cancelled the pending `setTimeout`/`requestAnimationFrame`, so a timer remained scheduled.

The fix tracks the actual frame handle (`frameHandle` + `frameIsRaf`) with a single `schedule()`/`clearFrame()` pair:
- `schedule()` only schedules when nothing is pending **and** animations remain, so natural end (map goes empty inside `tick`) leaves no timer.
- `cancel()` now clears the pending frame once the map is empty.
- `tick()` clears its own handle up front and reschedules only if work remains.

This satisfies all six controller requirements: synchronous first frame, continue on truthy (`{ keep: true }`) return, stop + removal on `null`, correct `running()` after end/cancel, restartable after cancel, and no leftover timers.

## Bug 2 — `LaserTrails.updateCollabTrails` (`packages/excalidraw/laser-trails.ts`)

The guard `if (!this.container || this.app.state.collaborators.size === 0) return;` bailed out **before** the cleanup loop whenever the collaborators map was empty — so when all remote collaborators were removed, their trail `<path>` elements were never detached from the SVG layer.

I dropped the `size === 0` condition. With an empty map the per-collaborator loop simply does nothing, and the cleanup loop now runs and removes every previously-rendered remote trail. The laser+down case is unaffected (size ≥ 1 always passed the old guard anyway), so a path element still appears for an active remote laser pointer.
